title: PAPER TIGERS
subtitle: Forgeries, funerals and a claw mark on every fake masterpiece
description: The art world's oldest lie is that a paper trail cannot kill. Appraisers in Jaipur, Delhi, Agra and Udaipur are dying and their collections are quietly being rewritten. Follow the claw mark, decode the provenance, and expose the forger hiding behind a perfect signature.

characters.name: Kalpana Bhatt
characters.bio: She could date a painting by its dust. Someone needed her to stop looking.

characters.name: Giovanni Price
characters.bio: Owned half the fakes he was ever shown - and knew about all of them.

characters.name: Asha Verma
characters.bio: Found the first fake idol and started asking whose hands touched it.

characters.name: Mohan Lal
characters.bio: His brush was his signature. Someone learned to copy it.

characters.name: Tabassum Rizvi
characters.bio: Kept the only honest index of the city's private collections.

characters.name: Vikrant Deo
characters.bio: He notarised a sale he should have refused. Then he called the police.

characters.name: Ratan Singh
characters.alibi: Hosting an opening night with a hundred guests and three photographers.
statements: You cannot forge what was never real to begin with.

characters.name: Sofia Alvarez
characters.alibi: In the conservation lab, logged in by keycard every twenty minutes.
statements: Restoring and faking are one skill apart.
The pigment on that canvas is younger than the story.

characters.name: Imtiaz Karim
characters.alibi: Teaching a masterclass to eighteen students, all filmed.
statements: A hand is a fingerprint. Mine is famous.
Someone is signing my name on work I never touched.

characters.name: Bianca Rossi
characters.alibi: Cleared customs in another country, stamps verified.
statements: I move pieces, I do not make them.

characters.name: Nusrat Jahan
characters.alibi: In a board meeting, minutes signed by seven trustees.
statements: Every fake in a museum started as a donation.
The thief always leaves the best paper behind.

characters.name: Jayant Mehra
characters.alibi: On the auction floor, on camera, for the entire evening.
statements: A provenance is only as honest as its notary.

characters.name: Lena Kovac
characters.alibi: Shooting a wedding portfolio, files timestamped to the minute.
statements: I photograph what is real. Then I print it twice.
The back of a canvas tells the truth.

characters.name: Hugo Meier
characters.alibi: Home, unreachable, phone switched off since the first death.
statements: I pay well and ask nothing.

characters.name: Ravi Chamar
characters.alibi: Loading a truck at the transport yard, weighbridge records confirm.
statements: Somebody recycles the same bubble wrap between galleries.

clues.name: The Claw Mark
clues.desc: Three parallel claw strokes branded into the frame. The Paper Tiger's calling card.

clues.name: The Triangle Mark
clues.desc: A neat triangle burned over the inventory number. The Ash Appraiser's mark.

clues.name: Forged Provenance
clues.desc: A certificate of origin with a museum stamp that closed forty years ago.

clues.name: Tiger Wax Seal
clues.desc: A private seal used to authenticate pieces. This one is a copy cast from the original.

clues.name: Saffron Ink Pot
clues.desc: The ink matches the signature on three questionable certificates.

clues.name: UV Lamp
clues.desc: A restorer's lamp, left charged. Under UV, half the signatures glow new.

clues.name: Acquisition Ledger
clues.desc: Fifty pieces bought for nothing and sold as heirlooms. Names are initialled.

clues.name: Rice-Paper Scrap
clues.desc: Torn from a rare scroll and tucked into a modern catalogue.

clues.name: Cotton Handling Gloves
clues.desc: Porter's gloves, dusted with the same pigment found on the fake.

clues.name: Restorer's Brush
clues.desc: A fine sable brush, still damp, with a thumbprint melted into the varnish.

clues.name: Stamped Passport
clues.desc: A dealer's passport with a page that should exist and does not.

clues.name: Ashes in an Envelope
clues.desc: Burned paperwork collected in a hurry. One corner survives: a bank account.

clues.name: Threatening Letter
clues.desc: Cut-out letters demanding a collection be 'corrected' before the auction.

clues.name: Packing Tape Roll
clues.desc: Gallery tape with a thread of antique silk stuck to the adhesive.

clues.name: Jeweller's Loupe
clues.desc: An auctioneer's loupe, left on the victim's desk after hours.

clues.name: Strongroom Key
clues.desc: A copy of the strongroom key, cut from a mould still in the workshop.

clues.name: Courier Invoice
clues.desc: A crate shipped to a silent buyer under a false description.

clues.name: Idol Shard
clues.desc: A broken fragment from a temple piece that was never supposed to leave.

clues.name: Auction Calendar
clues.desc: Circle marks on six dates, matching six pieces now in private hands.

clues.name: Donation Receipt
clues.desc: A temple donation receipt signed with a hand that appraises for a living.

clues.name: Appraiser's Diary
clues.desc: The last page lists three initials and the word 'owned'. No full names.

clues.name: Burner Phone
clues.desc: One number saved, labelled only with a camera brand. A photographer's spare.

clues.name: Train Ticket Stub
clues.desc: A first-class stub dated the night before the murder, seat 4A.

situationTemplates: {VICTIM}, {VICTIM_ROLE}, was found among crates in {CITY}. One crate had been opened and resealed.
An appraiser's office in {CITY}: {VICTIM}, {VICTIM_ROLE}, dead, with a catalogue open to a forged lot.
{VICTIM}, {VICTIM_ROLE}, cancelled an auction the morning they died. In {CITY}, the buyer is already calling.
briefingTemplates: The {MARK} was burned into the frame of a painting that should not exist. {MENACE} has been selling lies for years. Find the proof.
A forger needs quiet hands and an alibi with witnesses. {MENACE} has both. The {MARK} is the one habit they cannot quit.
{SUSPECT} was the last to appraise the piece. Sources say the paperwork is 'too perfect'. Find every clue before the auction clears.
